title: The Question Concerning a Particular Profound Boredom as the Fundamental Attunement of Our Contemporary Dasein

work.author: Martin Heidegger
work.title: The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics: World, Finitude, Solitude
work.german_title: Die Grundbegriffe der Metaphysik. Welt — Endlichkeit — Einsamkeit

structure.part: Part One — Awakening a Fundamental Attunement

locus_policy.ga_source: read from running heads, non-linear, never computed

one_sentence: Heidegger turns the formal analysis of profound boredom onto the contemporary age and diagnoses its fundamental attunement as an emptiness whose telling refusal is precisely the absence of any essential oppressiveness, against which the moment of vision is simultaneously announced as the latent, most extreme demand on Dasein.
abstract: Chapter Five (§§37–38) is the hinge that converts the impersonal, formal interpretation of the third (profound) form of boredom into a determinate diagnosis of 'our contemporary Dasein.' §37 reconsiders the guiding question — 'Has man in the end become boring to himself?' — reframing it not as an empirical survey of whether people today are bored by particular things but as a question of whether the Dasein in contemporary man is bored as such; it defends the demand 'not to counteract' boredom as a waiting that keeps to itself, and insists a question (not only an answer) can provide a hold. §38 questions in the two structural directions: (a) being-left-empty surfaces as the 'telling refusal of any essential oppressiveness' — the bustling self-defense against innumerable particular needs precisely prevents any need 'as a whole' from emerging, leaving a smug contentment in not-being-endangered; (b) being-held-in-limbo surfaces as the most extreme demand simultaneously announced in that very absence — the moment of vision (Augenblick) as the necessity of disclosive resolution by which Dasein takes itself up as its ownmost burden. The unit closes by handing the analysis to Part Two: the expanse of the 'as a whole' disclosed in profound boredom is named 'world.'

objects.label: a particular profound boredom of our contemporary Dasein
objects.note: Not profound boredom 'in general or universally' but one in particular — the boredom of our Dasein; superficial forms take their illumination from this essential boredom.

objects.label: the fundamental attunement of our contemporary Dasein
objects.note: The chapter's target: not 'where man stands' in world history but 'how things stand concerning the Da-sein in man.'

objects.label: Has man in the end become boring to himself?
objects.german: Ist der Mensch sich am Ende langweilig geworden?
objects.note: The reconsidered guiding question; first posed earlier (cf. p.77ff.), now repeated 'more transparently' after the formal analysis.

objects.label: not to counteract profound boredom
objects.note: Neither passivity nor bustling activity but 'this side of the two': Dasein's keeping-to-itself, which is a waiting directed toward essential questioning. Profound boredom 'only becomes awake if we do not counteract it.'

objects.label: a question is able to provide a hold
objects.note: Against common understanding and 'programmaticism,' which grant a hold only to the answer (a fixed proposition, dogma, conviction).

objects.label: being left empty
objects.note: Here specified: being delivered over to beings' telling refusal of themselves as a whole — an emptiness as a whole, not a pure Nothing but emptiness as telling refusal / self-withdrawal / lack / deprivation / need (Not).

objects.label: being held in limbo
objects.note: Here specified: being impelled toward the extremity of that which makes Dasein possible — toward the moment of vision; the demand simultaneously announced in the telling refusal.

objects.label: telling refusal
objects.note: Beings as a whole withhold themselves yet in withholding announce what is refused 'in all its harshness'; the refusal is itself a kind of telling that here remains inaudible.

objects.label: need
objects.note: Emptiness 'in the sense of telling refusal … thus emptiness as lack, deprivation, need [Not]'; the deepest need is that an essential oppressiveness refuses itself.

objects.label: the absence of any essential oppressiveness
objects.note: The keystone diagnosis: what oppresses us most profoundly and in a concealed manner is precisely the very absence of any essential oppressiveness in our Dasein as a whole; this absence is 'the fundamental emptiness that bores us.'

objects.label: oppressiveness
objects.note: Glossed against bedrängt (to oppress, press hard). The need in question is not that this or that need 'oppresses [bedrängt]' but that an essential oppressiveness [Bedrängnis] is absent.

objects.label: bustling self-defense against the needs of Dasein
objects.note: The contemporary reaction — organizations, programs, parties — confirms the particular needs yet 'precisely does not allow any need to emerge as a whole'; particular needs are therefore no proof of emptiness as a whole.

objects.label: universal smug contentment in not being endangered
objects.note: Attested by the very restlessness with which we busy ourselves; makes us believe we no longer need to be strong in the ground of our essence; 'learned competencies' cannot replace strength.

objects.label: the mystery is lacking in our Dasein
objects.note: With the absent mystery [Geheimnis], the 'inner terror' every mystery carries — which gives Dasein its greatness — also remains absent.

objects.label: the moment of vision
objects.note: Simultaneously announced in the telling refusal; the look of resolute disclosedness of Dasein for its Da-sein; to be seized 'as the innermost necessity of the freedom of Dasein'; not a fixed ideal but that which must wrest its own possibility from itself again.

objects.label: the most extreme demand made upon man
objects.note: Commensurate with emptiness as a whole; not an arbitrary demand but 'the demand pure and simple' — that Dasein as such is demanded of man, 'given to him — to be there.'

objects.label: the necessity of disclosive resolution
objects.note: Man must 'resolutely open himself again to this demand'; the moment of vision must time and again stand before Dasein as that which is properly binding — distinguished from the haste/abruptness of programs that masquerade as resolute disclosedness.

objects.label: loading Dasein upon man as his ownmost burden
objects.note: Liberation of the Dasein in man is not arbitrary positioning but burdening; 'only those who can truly give themselves a burden are free.' Man must in each case 'throw Dasein upon his shoulders.'

objects.label: the oscillation between the expanse of emptiness and the extremity of the moment of vision
objects.note: Cannot be objectively ascertained or registered as a matter of fact; this oscillation is the temporal structure of the particular profound boredom — we 'can only ask' whether it attunes our Dasein through and through.

objects.label: concealing Dasein from itself through psychology
objects.note: Contemporary man may suppress profound boredom 'in spite of all his psychology and psychoanalysis, indeed precisely through psychology, which today even presents itself as depth psychology.'

objects.label: the courage of mood
objects.note: Questioning concerning the fundamental attunement is where it can be decided whether we can 'summon the courage of mood [Mut]' for what this attunement gives us to know; the word it speaks 'summons us to action and to being.'

objects.label: the expanse of the 'as a whole' designated as world
objects.note: The Part One → Part Two hinge: what we ought to find oppressive is the absence of oppressiveness — 'the very expanse of this emptiness as a whole,' which 'manifests itself in profound boredom,' designated as world.

objects.label: §18c first naming of profound boredom
objects.note: Earlier reference point: profound boredom first named the concealed fundamental attunement of the contemporary situation at p.74; Ch.5 cashes out and concretizes that naming.

claims: The question 'Has man become boring to himself?' cannot be answered by asking whether contemporary people are bored by particular things or more bored than in other epochs; it asks only whether the Dasein in contemporary man is bored as such.

Profound boredom only becomes awake if we do not counteract it; 'not counteracting' is neither passivity nor bustling activity but Dasein's keeping-to-itself, a waiting directed toward essential questioning.

Being-left-empty in the contemporary case is the telling refusal of any essential oppressiveness: the bustling self-defense against countless particular needs precisely prevents any need 'as a whole' from emerging.
What oppresses us most profoundly and in a concealed manner is precisely the absence of any essential oppressiveness — this absence is the fundamental emptiness that bores us.

Being-held-in-limbo is the most extreme demand simultaneously announced in that very absence: the moment of vision (Augenblick) as the necessity of disclosive resolution, by which Dasein takes itself up as its ownmost burden.

The oscillation between the expanse of emptiness and the extremity of the moment of vision cannot be ascertained as a matter of fact; we 'can only ask' whether it attunes contemporary Dasein through and through.
The expanse of the 'as a whole' that manifests itself in profound boredom is designated as world, opening Part Two's question 'What is world?'

boredom_bridge.summary: This unit supplies the bridge's diagnostic register: profound boredom as a concrete attunement of a determinate (contemporary) Dasein, structured as being-left-empty (telling refusal) in unity with being-held-in-limbo (the moment of vision as demand). Its keystone contribution is the figure of an emptiness that refuses — a hollowness masked by surface busyness — which underwrites the King–Salvo second-form reading (surface gaze occupied / depth attunement hollow) and the methodological caution that profound boredom 'cannot be ascertained' as a present-at-hand matter of fact.
